title: Early Renewal of Web Hosting Plans at Checkout
content:
**Web Hosting Plans — renewing at checkout while the current term is running**

**Scope.** This pricing governs a renewal that the account holder pays at Harborline's checkout for a plan whose term end date is later than today and which carries no scheduled downgrade or term change request, and only such a renewal. A renewal that the account holder pays at Harborline's checkout for a plan whose term end date is on or before today and which carries no scheduled downgrade request is priced by Harborline's overdue renewal pricing. Every other renewal — an auto-renew charge, a renewal that applies a scheduled downgrade request, or a renewal paid at checkout while the term end date is later than today for a plan with a scheduled term change request — is billed at the regular rate of the tier and term length that the new term will have (the regular 12, 24 or 36-month rate multiplied by the months, or the 1-month price for a 1-month term, with no setup fee), less the account tier's hosting discount percentage, rounded half up to the cent.

**Who pays.** The early renewal is the account holder's own payment, completed at Harborline's checkout by card or through PayPal after the agent quotes the amount, because Harborline support never takes payment details; a payment from account credit is not taken under this rule.

**Conditions.** A renewal may be charged only while the plan status is active or suspended. A scheduled downgrade is applied at renewal only when the websites in use and the storage used fit within the target tier's websites allowance and storage, which concerns only a renewal that applies a scheduled downgrade request and therefore never an early renewal under this rule. The new term always starts on the previous term end date.

**When it is billed.** An early renewal is not billed until the plan's term start date is on or before today. While the plan's term start date is later than today, no early renewal is billed.

### Checkout tool: `pay_hosting_renewal_early_31233d6b`

The agent unlocks this customer-side tool and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it to pay the renewal. A manual renewal line covering the next term is recorded on the plan. The next term begins on the current term end date and runs for the stated number of months: the plan's term dates move to that next term, its billing term becomes the stated length and the introductory-term flag is cleared; the auto-renew setting is left as it is.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `hosting_id` | Reference number of the customer's hosting plan being renewed, as given to the customer by the agent from the hosting plan lookup. |
| `amount` | Renewal amount paid, USD, positive, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent. |
| `term_months` | Length of the next term in calendar months: an integer that is one of the offered terms 1, 12, 24 or 36. |
| `payment_method` | `card` (charged to the customer's payment card) or `paypal` (paid through the customer's PayPal account). |

**Return.** On success: status "renewed", `hosting_charge_id` (the renewal line), `order_ref` (HL- followed by 8 digits), `amount`, `term_months`, `term_start_date` and `term_end_date` (the next term's dates) and `payment_method`. The customer sees the renewal line with its own order number and the plan's new term end date.

**Errors.** The tool refuses a payment method other than card or PayPal, a term other than 1, 12, 24 or 36 months, an unknown plan and an amount that is not positive.
